json_escape.what: escape_json of one fixed string (4 fixed inputs cycled incl. quotes, backslash, control chars, 80000 iters per rep)

lsn_parse_format.what: parse+format round-trip of one fixed LSN string (8 fixed inputs cycled, 160000 iters per rep)

native_int32_codec.what: big-endian int32 write+read of one value (20.48M iters per rep over a 1024-entry buffer)

environment: Linux VM (shared, ~1.5 effective CPU, 7.9 GB RAM), gcc 13.3.0
framework: standalone C harness (perf/bench.c, gcc -O2 -std=gnu11, CLOCK_MONOTONIC, warmup + 5 reps, fixed inputs/iterations)
notes: HIGH VARIANCE: the shared VM was under heavy parallel load during the 2026-11-21 rollout. Run means across 6 runs: lsn_parse_format 137-372 ns, json_escape 139-451 ns, native_int32_codec 4.2-7.3 ns. Baseline is the median of those run means. Treat single reruns against the 10%/25% thresholds as noisy; re-run several times and compare medians before acting on a warn/block.
scope: EXTRACTED pure-C kernels only: the original extension cannot be built here - verified 2026-11-21: `which pg_config` exits 1, /usr/lib/postgresql absent, ~/.pgrx absent, and every src/*.c includes postgres.h. Kernels: (1) LSN parse/format, the pg_lsn_in/out algorithm used by str_to_lsn() in src/spock_common.c; (2) JSON escaping, escape_json() semantics used in src/spock_change_log.c; (3) native-protocol big-endian int32 codec, pqformat primitives used by src/spock_proto_native.c. NOT covered: apply/output-plugin/replication paths, which need a live PostgreSQL cluster (tests/regress + tests/tap).
